 Print Schools in parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal have been closed on October 26 amid heavy rainfall and cyclone-related weather warnings. Schools in Dindigul and Coimbatore districts of Tamil Nadu will remain closed on October 26 as heavy rainfall and cyclone-related weather conditions disrupt normal life. Puducherry and Karaikal have also declared a holiday for schools and colleges today according to media reports. The closures come as Cyclone Arnab is expected to develop over the Bay of Bengal and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. The holiday declarations follow persistent rainfall, waterlogging, and disruptions to road transport in affected areas. District administrations have taken precautionary measures to protect students and school staff. However, the closures are not statewide, and parents should check announcements from their respective district administrations before sending children to school. Schools and colleges in Chengalpattu district are scheduled to function as usual. Tamil Nadu school holiday: District-wise status
 The school holiday announcements for October 26 vary across Tamil Nadu, depending on local weather conditions and administrative orders. Dindigul : Schools will remain closed on Monday due to heavy rainfall.
 Coimbatore : Schools will remain closed in view of the prevailing weather conditions.
 The Nilgiris : Schools in Udhagamandalam, Coonoor, Kotagiri and Kundah taluks have been included in the closure announcements.
 Theni : Schools in Periyakulam taluk will remain closed.
 Chengalpattu : Schools and colleges will function as usual, according to the district administration.
 Chennai : Parents should follow official district announcements for confirmation of any change in school timings or operations.
 The closures apply to the areas covered by the respective orders. Students and parents should not assume that schools across Tamil Nadu have been shut for the day. Puducherry, Karaikal, schools and colleges closed
 The Puducherry administration has declared a holiday for schools and colleges in Puducherry and Karaikal on October 26 due to heavy rainfall and cyclone-related weather warnings. The closure covers government, government-aided and private educational institutions. Waterlogging in low-lying areas and disruption to road traffic have added to concerns over the safety of students travelling to educational institutions. Parents have been advised to follow official announcements from the administration and their respective schools for further updates. Cyclone Arnab: Heavy rain warning continues
 Cyclone Arnab is expected to intensify over the Bay of Bengal before moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. The weather system has prompted authorities to monitor conditions along the eastern coast, with heavy rainfall forecast in several parts of Tamil Nadu. The IMD has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places in parts of the state. Persistent downpours could lead to waterlogging, traffic disruption and unsafe travel conditions in vulnerable areas. The situation remains subject to change as the weather system develops. District administrations may review school operations based on rainfall and local conditions. Will online classes be held during the school holiday?
 Schools may consider online lessons or homework where feasible, depending on their arrangements. However, parents should confirm the instructions issued by individual institutions rather than assume that online classes will be conducted during the closure. School authorities have also been advised to avoid offline assemblies, special classes and remedial sessions during closure periods. Will examinations be postponed?
 The closure of schools does not automatically mean that scheduled board or university examinations have been postponed. Students appearing for public examinations or university examinations should check notifications issued by the respective examination authorities. Parents and students should avoid flooded roads, stormwater drains and waterlogged underpasses. They should also follow official district administration channels for updated school holiday announcements and weather advisories.
